statement: HBM memory remains supply-constrained with suppliers keeping pricing power: HBM4 contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027 (from ~$2 to $4-5 per gigabit), while HBM consumes ~3x the wafer capacity of DDR5, carries 4-6 month production cycles and low initial yields, and is projected to reach ~30% of total DRAM production capacity.
why: Long-term contracts tying up 20-30% of general DRAM capacity, longer HBM4 cycles and low yields keep memory tight while demand from Nvidia's HBM4-based Vera Rubin (H2 2027) builds, so suppliers retain pricing power.

impact.mechanism: Tight HBM capacity and doubling prices lift memory-maker revenue and margins (positive for HBM) but raise the bill-of-materials cost and constrain the memory supply feeding merchant AI GPUs.

evidence.excerpt: memory suppliers retain pricing power; HBM tightness intensifies through 2026 into 2027 with prices set to roughly double

confidence.basis: Single secondary trade-press source relaying analyst forecasts; no primary filing.
